property_summary: After calling go with a positive value, the contract C forwards all received Ether to owner (so address(c).balance == 0), i.e. go never leaves leftover balance.

When go is called with any positive value, the original contract always reverts if the external call to target fails to send the funds, whereas the mutant continues; thus for the original, go never returns successfully when the call to target fails.
For all inputs, if go(...) returns successfully (does not revert) then address(c).balance == 0 afterwards (no leftover Ether kept in the contract).
If calling go(...) succeeds (does not revert) then the call to the external target also succeeded.

If go(...) returns successfully when called with a positive amount, then address(this).balance must not increase (meaning C forwarded all funds out, so the call did not fail), i.e., successful return implies no leftover Ether kept by C causing the caller to receive nothing.

For any caller and any wei amount, when the callee address reverts on receiving funds the reference C will forward the leftover balance to owner (so contract balance is 0 after go()), whereas the mutant inverts the require and will keep funds in the contract for some inputs (failing callee), so address(c).balance == 0 always for the reference but can be >0 for the mutant.

For any caller and any payable amount sent to go(), the correct contract C always ends with address(c).balance == 0 (it forwards leftover funds to owner after the external call); the mutant that inverts the require can leave funds in the contract for some inputs (when the external call fails), making address(c).balance > 0.

For any caller and any ETH amount sent to go(), the reference C always leaves its own balance zero after go() (it forwards any leftover funds to owner); the mutant that inverts the require can keep funds in the contract when the external call fails, violating address(c).balance == 0 for some inputs.

For every caller and every amount, calling go() on the correct contract either succeeds (when the external call to target returns true) or reverts (when that call returns false); the mutant inverts the require, so for some adversarial callee behaviours the success/revert outcome flips — we assert that go() succeeds exactly when the external target call succeeds.

For every call to go() where the external target call succeeds (callee accepts funds), the reference contract forwards all remaining balance out and finishes without reverting; the mutant inverts the require and therefore will revert when the external call succeeds — so the property: whenever the target accepts (i.e. does not revert) calling go() on the reference must succeed (not revert).

For every call to go() that successfully forwards msg.value to an external target, the reference contract always forwards any remaining contract balance back to owner (so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards); the mutant removes that final transfer so for some inputs (when target accepts but leaves balance in c) address(c).balance != 0.

For every admissible call to go(value) where the callee accepts the forwarded value, the reference contract always ends with zero balance (it forwards any remaining balance back to owner); the mutant that removes the final transfer can leave non-zero contract balance for some inputs (when the callee accepts but does not drain the contract), so address(c).balance != 0 for some fuzzed value.

For every call to go(value) where the external target accepts the forwarded ETH (call succeeds), the reference contract always ends with zero balance (it forwards any remaining balance back to owner); the mutant that removes the final transfer can leave a non-zero contract balance for some inputs where the callee accepts funds but does not drain the contract.

For any call to go(amount) where the external target accepts the forwarded ETH (call succeeds), the reference contract always ends with zero balance (it forwards any remaining balance back to owner); the mutant that removes the final transfer can leave a non-zero contract balance for some inputs where the callee accepts funds but does not drain the contract.

For every call to go(amount) where the external target accepts the forwarded ETH (call succeeds), the reference contract always ends with zero balance (it forwards any remaining contract balance back to owner); the mutant that removes the final transfer can leave a non-zero contract balance when the callee accepts funds but does not drain the contract.

For every call to go() sending any amount from any caller, the contract's owner (owner getter) must always receive any leftover balance from C so that C.balance == 0 after the call; the mutant that transfers leftover funds to msg.sender can leave owner unpaid and thus violate that C.balance == 0 relative to owner receiving leftover funds.

For every caller and value, after go(...) returns the contract's balance must be zero (all ether forwarded to the intended recipient), but the mutant that sends leftover funds to msg.sender can leave owner unpaid causing address(c).balance or owner not receiving funds — detect by checking address(c).balance == 0 after call through an adversarial callee that accepts then drains leftovers to caller in mutant.

For any caller and any sent value where the external target call succeeds but does NOT pull any further funds from the contract, the reference always ensures that any leftover balance is forwarded to the contract owner (so address(c).balance == 0 after go); the mutant forwards leftovers to msg.sender instead and thus can leave owner unpaid or leave different balances, causing address(c).balance or owner balance behavior to differ.

For any caller and any value where the external target call succeeds, the contract forwards its remaining balance to the stored owner (so owner balance increases by any leftover); the mutant forwards leftovers to msg.sender instead and thus can leave owner not receiving those funds for some inputs.

For any caller and any value sent to go(), if the external static target call succeeds, the reference contract always forwards its remaining balance to the stored owner (so address(c).balance == 0 after go returns), while the mutant that transfers leftover to msg.sender will, for some caller/value combinations, not leave the contract with zero balance for the owner (observable via address(c).balance or differing balances); we test that address(c).balance == 0 always holds for the reference but is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any caller and any positive ETH value sent to go, the reference forwards exactly that ETH value out to the external target (so the contract's balance returns to its pre-call level); the mutant forwards zero instead and thus the contract keeps the sent ETH, increasing its balance — violating the rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any ETH amount sent to go, the correct contract forwards the entire msg.value to its external target so address(c).balance does not increase; the mutant forwards 0 and thus address(c).balance increases for some inputs (a positive msg.value sent by any externally-owned caller).

For any external caller and any positive ETH value sent to go(), the reference contract forwards the entire msg.value to the external target so address(c).balance does not increase; the mutant forwards 0 causing address(c).balance to increase for some positive msg.value sent, breaking this property.

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value, calling go forwards that exact value to the external target so the contract's balance after the call equals its balance before the call (i.e., address(c).balance does not increase); the mutant forwards 0 instead and thus for some positive msg.value the contract's balance increases, violating this rule.
